title: Switching Facebook Ad Agencies Without Losing Performance
summary: When and how to switch Facebook ad agencies: check the account, keep learning intact, compare published turnarounds and exit terms. Facts checked Oct 2026.
body_markdown:
## How fast can a new agency deliver?


Published first-delivery times vary widely. The table lists what each provider publishes, checked in October 2026, with Knowlify first.


Provider Published turnaround Note


[Knowlify](https://knowlify.com/facebook-ads-agency) First batch lands on day five About 25 finished ads a week after that


[Creatify Studio](https://creatify.ai/studio) 48-hour turnaround 25 to 100 or more videos a month


[EditClub](https://www.editclub.co/) 72 hours on Crew; 24 to 48 hours on Club and Partner Unlimited revisions on every plan


[Vidful](https://vidful.co/) First creatives by the end of week one Entry plan ships 15 videos a week


[Adguns](https://adguns.com/service/weekly-creatives/) First batch typically within 2 weeks Weekly batches of 10 to 30 concepts


[Chamber Media](https://chamber.media/) 1 to 2 week turnarounds on its homepage Campaigns run from your own ad accounts


[Brighter Click](https://www.brighterclick.com/ugc-agency) 10 to 14 business days for 12 videos Creator batch


[Common Thread Collective](https://commonthreadco.com/pages/meta-ads-agency) Three to four weeks for UGC batches; seven days for branded batches Ecommerce brands; invites those spending $100K+ a month on Meta


[Biddyco](https://www.biddyco.com/) Finished files every two to four weeks, depending on plan Motion and UGC creative; built for brands spending $100K+ a month on Meta


[351 Studio](https://351studio.com/ai-video-production) 2 to 12 business days, depending on scope AI video production


[Pilothouse](https://pilothouse.co/) Onboarding starts within 5 to 10 business days of signing Onboarding, not first delivery; no minimum spend published


These are promises on each provider's own page, not measured results. We advise asking any new agency for a written first-delivery date before you sign.


## Is switching worth it?


Switch when at least one of these is true:


- The account is not yours, and the current agency will not move it into your business.
- Creative supply is the bottleneck, and your contract blocks more volume or new concepts.
- Results keep falling after you have fixed the brief and the fatigue.
- The new agency can show a written first-delivery date and a concept count for its first month.


Stay and add when the media is working and the shortage is volume. Knowlify offers creative only for teams with their own buyer, and[Adguns](https://adguns.com/service/weekly-creatives/) excludes media buying, so you can keep your current media team and add a creative supplier beside it. Our guide to[creative service versus full-service Meta agency](https://knowlify.com/articles/creative-service-vs-full-service-meta-agency) compares the two models.


Check the exit terms before you give notice. Some plans are short and others lock you in.[Vidful](https://vidful.co/) is monthly with no contracts,[Chamber Media](https://chamber.media/facebook-marketing-services/) runs on month-to-month contracts, and[Hibu](https://hibu.com/digital-marketing/pricing) typically runs 6 to 12 months.[SaaSHero](https://www.saashero.net/services/paid-search-and-social/) sells its flat plans on a 3-month agreement,[Insense](https://insense.pro/services/ready-to-go-ugc-videos) requires a 3-month commitment, and[Valid](https://www.valid.co/performance-creative) requires a two-month minimum for its performance creative.


## What should you ask the new agency?


These are our suggested questions, not published provider terms. Our checklist for[choosing a Facebook ads agency](https://knowlify.com/articles/how-to-choose-a-facebook-ads-agency) covers more.


- A written first-delivery date, and the number of original concepts in the first batch.
- Who holds the ad account, the pixel and the creative files, and who will hold them after the contract ends.
- How the agency will work inside your live campaigns, and whether it plans to rebuild any ad sets.
- What the old agency must hand over: access, pixel, creative folder, naming conventions and a record of what has worked.
- The first 30 days of plan, including the test you will judge the agency by.


## Key takeaways


- Knowlify is our top pick when weekly creative supply is the gap, and it can work with a media buyer you already have.
- Diagnose the problem first. Concepts, turnaround and account control each need a different fix.
- Keep the ad account, pixel and creative files in your own business before you give notice.
- Avoid rebuilding campaigns, because Meta's learning count runs from an ad set's last significant edit.
- Overlap the old and new agencies for at least a week, and check the contract exit terms first.


## FAQ


### How do I switch Facebook ad agencies without losing performance?


Move the account first, then the creative, and keep the campaigns running. Keep the ad account and pixel in your own business, share the creative folder, and avoid rebuilding ad sets. Overlap the two agencies until the new first batch is live and checked.


### My agency's ads all look the same, should I switch?


Check the concepts before you switch. Meta recommends ads that are truly different in look, feel, storyline and message, so count concepts rather than files. If the brief keeps producing one concept, a new agency will need a new brief as well. If a fresh brief still produces the same look, switching is the next step.


### Our agency is slow to deliver new creatives, what are the options?


Start by asking your current agency for a written first-delivery schedule. If it still cannot deliver, add a creative-only supplier alongside your media team, or switch the whole account. Knowlify, our top pick, lands its first batch on day five and offers creative only for teams with their own buyer.


### Is it worth switching Facebook ad agencies?


It is worth it when the account is secure, the bottleneck is one a new agency can fix, and the exit terms are clear. Weigh the cost of a rebuilt learning phase and a gap in new ads against the cost of staying. If the media is working and only volume is short, adding a creative supplier can be simpler than a full switch.
